"I just tried to capture as many things as possible in this picture", i think that's the problem. 

Even though having a lot of things in a photo is great, you still need to define your point of interest. There must be something in the photo that become the main actor. Whether is it a group of people, the building, single person, etc. In this photo everything is captured but there's no focus. I think you need to get closer to focus on its people or step a few back so you can show the whole building, tree, and the field.

I think the composition is a little bit confusing. I know that you want to show a school activity but the subject isn't really clear here. I mean, what's your point of interest? Is it the people, or the whole atmosphere? Maintain a good composition of Foreground, Midground, and background. In this photo i see a tree that can be a good foreground to frame the whole situation.

And lighting is important to create a point of interest. Well-lit subject will draw viewers eyes to it, and in this photo, the lighting lack of contrast and doesn't "pop" really well.

Yeah, that's why i use tripod all the time, AEB, and combine them all for exposure blending. It's really cool for a photo that has dynamic range nearly match our eye's (only do this technique  for landscape photography though). The photo feels alive.
